channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: How AI is Accelerating Cyberattacks
item.description: The number of cyberattacks spiked in 2020 and has remained elevated since, posing a threat to the businesses, infrastructure, and critical systems we depend on. Experts say AI has played a role in both accelerating attacks and defending against them, but it gives criminals the upper hand. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s AI Agent War, Early 2027 Product Plans and iPhone Duo Face Unlock Review
item.description: Also: The company prepares a slew of new iPhones, iPads and Macs for early 2027.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Nvidia Board Faces a Governance Reckoning
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg opinion columnist Gautam Mukunda tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has exposed broader corporate governance problems, as the board faces outside pressure to bring him back while investigations and potential shareholder litigation loom. Mukunda argues that Silicon Valley’s tendency to concentrate power around founder CEOs can weaken oversight, while Huang’s exit also complicates the debate over whether the US should allow advanced Nvidia chips to be sold to China. Nvidia has publicly said its board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Outages Fuel a New Prepping Boom
item.description: Bloomberg senior cybersecurity reporter Jordan Robertson tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a wave of network failures resembling the effects of a major cyberattack was instead self-inflicted, exposing risks from aging infrastructure, interconnected systems, staffing cuts and the rapid adoption of AI. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Robertson explains why the disruptions are fueling renewed interest in doomsday prepping while cautioning that a prolonged cyber catastrophe remains unlikely. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Governors Call for Federal AI Rules Without Sidelining States
item.description: A bipartisan group of US governors is urging Washington to set rules for the most powerful artificial intelligence systems while allowing states to protect consumers, workers and children from the technology’s risks.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Gray and Michael B. Marois

item.title: Tower Records Becomes Latest Japan Retailer Hit by Data Breach
item.description: Music retailer Tower Records Japan Inc. said customer information was leaked following unauthorized access, making it the nation’s latest retailer to disclose a data breach.
item.dc:creator: Min Jeong Lee and Takahiko Hyuga

item.title: China Objects to US Curbs on Telecoms’ Access to Phone Numbers
item.description: China urged the US to withdraw a measure barring its three largest telecoms from directly obtaining US phone numbers, saying the action violates principles of nondiscrimination and fair competition.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Australia Spy Chief Warns of Data Center, AI Risks, Age Reports
item.description: Australia’s spy chief said that data centers and artificial intelligence risk exposing the nation to foreign interference and malicious state actors, according to an interview in The Age Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Amy Bainbridge

item.title: Crowdstrike’s Talks With Zscaler Show AI-Led Cyber Consolidation
item.description: A wave of multibillion-dollar takeovers is reshaping the cybersecurity industry as the biggest companies race to expand their defenses against increasingly sophisticated attacks powered by artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Robertson

item.title: California Nvidia Probe Covers Potential Criminal Law Violations
item.description: California’s probe into whether Nvidia Corp. illegally sold advanced chips to China and misled investors about the conduct is also looking at potential criminal violations of state law, raising the stakes for the chipmaker.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson
